## One document, several elements

A Quarto note can combine an explanation, mathematical notation, and code.

## An equation

The sample mean is

$$
\bar{x}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i.
$$

For the observations below, $\bar{x}=(2+4+6)/3=4$.

| Observation | Value |
|---|---:|
| 1 | 2 |
| 2 | 4 |
| 3 | 6 |

## R code

This example displays the code without executing it, so the template can be
rendered before R and its packages are configured.

```r
x <- c(2, 4, 6)
mean(x)
```

The expected result is `4`. To execute this chunk, install R and the `knitr`
and `rmarkdown` packages, change the opening fence from ` ```r ` to
` ```{r} ` (without the spaces), add `#| eval: true` as the first line inside
the chunk, and render again. The output will then be calculated and included in the page.

## A useful check

Compare the computed result with the hand calculation. If they differ,
check the observations, missing values, and the function arguments.
